title: Deterministic Text Readability
instructions:
Implement two helper functions and `TextStats` in `text_stats.py`. Use the exact mechanical
rules below, not a linguistic library. All text arguments are strings.

`words(text: str) -> list[str]` returns lowercase matches of ASCII pattern
`[A-Za-z]+(?:'[A-Za-z]+)*`, in order. Only a straight apostrophe joins letters. Digits,
hyphens, curly apostrophes, and non-ASCII characters are separators.

`syllables(word: str) -> int` requires a full match of that word pattern, otherwise raises
`ValueError`. Lowercase and remove apostrophes. Count maximal runs of vowels `aeiouy`.
If the resulting word has more than two letters, ends in `e` but not `le`, and the count
is greater than one, subtract one. Return at least one. Examples: make=1, table=2, sky=1,
queue=1, rhythm=1. This heuristic intentionally does not model all English pronunciation.

`TextStats(text: str = '')` stores text. Its public methods are:
- `replace(text: str) -> None`: replace all stored text.
- `append(text: str) -> None`: append exactly as supplied, with NO inserted separator.
- `summary() -> dict`: return exactly `words`, `sentences`, `syllables`, `characters`,
  `reading_ease`. Words and syllables are totals from the helpers. Sentences are chunks
  split by one or more `.`, `!`, or `?` that contain at least one word; a final unterminated
  chunk counts too. Thus punctuation-only chunks never count. Characters is Python len
  of the entire original text, including whitespace and punctuation. Reading ease is
  `round(206.835 - 1.015 * words / sentences - 84.6 * syllables / words, 2)`; use 0.0
  when there are no words. Do not clamp scores. Summary is a fresh dictionary.
- `most_common(limit: int = 5) -> list[tuple[str, int]]`: word frequencies sorted by
  descending count, then ascending word. Require a nonnegative integer excluding bool,
  else `ValueError`; zero returns [].
All methods reflect the latest text, including after edits; no stale cached counts.

## Files
- `text_stats.py`
